findings.hypothesis: Nearly all of the created->confirmed loss is concentrated in 'instant' consults: instant requests convert at ~51.8% and account for essentially the entire top_gap (≈87.5k lost). This implies the primary mechanism is matching/availability or automated cancellation of instant routing rather than payment entry UI for the majority of lost requests.
findings.confirm_via: Run an A/B experiment on instant requests: treatment A shows expanded doctor availability (incentivize acceptance or enlarge matching window) or an immediate scheduled-fallback option; treatment B is current flow. Measure confirmed conversion and log acceptance / timeout reasons. A large lift in treatment A would confirm routing/availability as causal.

findings.hypothesis: The low created->confirmed conversion also concentrates in the online delivery channel (50.19%); this overlaps with instant requests and points to the online matching/acceptance path (chat/video marketplace) as the locus of failures.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab conversion for consultation_trigger x delivery_channel (instant & online vs other combos). Instrument the online matching flow to record exact failure mode (no doctor available / timed out / server error). If instant+online has much higher timeout/auto-cancel rates than instant via other channels, that confirms the online matching path as the mechanism.

findings.hypothesis: A large portion of created requests are 'cash' and cash converts at only ~46.5%; this could reflect a payment/payer verification or flow difference (e.g., users selecting cash then not completing an acceptance or verification step) that increases auto-cancels, or it could be that cash requests are the same instant/online cohort with low acceptance.
findings.confirm_via: Run a stratified analysis or experiment controlling for consultation_trigger and delivery_channel (compare instant+online cash vs instant+online wallet/insurance). If cash remains worse after controlling, test a small holdout that requires an immediate wallet pre-auth or soft-verify to see if confirmed conversion increases.

evidence: user_reasons: abandoned from the patient selection screen 4134
findings.hypothesis: Large counts of 'abandoned by system' (54,015) and 'abandoned from the patient selection screen' (4,134) indicate many cancellations are automated or timeouts during routing/doctor selection, consistent with a matching/availability failure mode rather than manual user cancellation.
findings.confirm_via: Instrument server logs and the patient-selection flow to map each 'abandoned by system' to the precise trigger (doctor reject, no-match timeout, backend error). Also run a pilot increasing selection timeout or providing a fallback to scheduled and measure reduction in system-abandoned events.

findings.hypothesis: Web clients convert much worse (35.59%) than mobile (iOS 63.63%, Android 60.77%), so a portion of the loss is client-specific (session/API differences, payment widget or UX) that causes higher drop or timeouts on web.
findings.confirm_via: A/B test a streamlined web flow (simpler patient-selection UI, keep-alive heartbeats, or prompt to continue in-app) versus current web flow and measure created->confirmed conversion. Also inspect web-side logs for network/session timeouts matching 'abandoned by system' events.

growth_ideas.title: Instant->Scheduled fallback with ETA
growth_ideas.rationale: Most of the created->confirmed loss sits in instant/online requests (instant entered 181651 converted 94141 rate 0.5183) and many cancellations are automated (abandoned by system 54015). Offering an immediate, explicit fallback to the earliest scheduled slot + an ETA should convert users who would otherwise be auto-cancelled.
growth_ideas.description: When an instant request cannot find/confirm a doctor within N seconds (e.g., 20–30s), show the user an explicit choice: (A) wait with a displayed ETA and confirm when a doctor accepts, or (B) book the earliest scheduled slot (show exact time) and immediately confirm. If the user chooses B, create a scheduled booking and skip the instant matching path.

growth_ideas.title: Reserve slot with small refundable token
growth_ideas.rationale: High automated abandons (54,015) and low cash conversion (cash rate 0.4653) suggest users and providers both need a stronger reservation signal. A small refundable token (wallet or card pre-auth) reduces no-shows and increases provider willingness to accept instant matches.
growth_ideas.description: Offer users an opt-in 'reserve' button on instant requests that places a refundable token (small wallet charge or pre-auth) to signal commitment and prioritize their request to doctors; refund automatically if auto-cancelled. Add UI explaining refund to maintain user trust.

growth_ideas.title: Web quick-path + app deep-link prompt
growth_ideas.rationale: Web conversion is very low (web entered 18101 converted 6443 rate 0.3559). A simplified one-screen web quick-path and an option to continue in-app (deep-link) should reduce web-specific abandonment and timeouts.
growth_ideas.description: Deploy a condensed web flow for consult requests that reduces steps (single patient-selection + single confirm) and shows an 'Open in App' deep-link button for users with the app installed. Track created->confirmed on web quick-path vs baseline.
